title: Admin Dashboard Data Flow
purpose: Show how the admin dashboard aggregates platform-wide metrics from 5 parallel Promise.all queries with no caching layer
audience: Backend developers, admin frontend developers, platform maintainers, performance engineers
description: When an admin navigates to the dashboard, the frontend calls GET /api/v1/admin/dashboard which passes through protectAndAdmin middleware (JWT validation + admin role check). The admin controller calls admin.service.getDashboardStats(), which executes 5 parallel queries via Promise.all(): UserModel.countAllUsers (total user count), UserModel.countActiveCreators (active creators count), TransactionModel.sumPlatformFeeForPeriod(30) (platform revenue last 30 days), SupportTicketModel.countOpenTickets (open and pending ticket count), and UserModel.getNewUsersOverTime(6) (monthly user signup trend for last 6 months). All 5 queries run concurrently. The results are assembled into a response object with keyMetrics and userGrowth that the frontend renders as 5 cards/charts. Issues: no caching (runs 5 queries every page load), no error isolation (Promise.all rejects entirely if one query fails), and sumPlatformFeeForPeriod scans transactions table with no index on created_at.

nodes.label: Admin Navigates to Dashboard
nodes.description: Admin clicks Dashboard in admin panel navigation.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/admin/dashboard
nodes.description: Frontend sends GET request to admin dashboard endpoint.

nodes.label: protectAndAdmin Middleware
nodes.description: JWT validation + admin role check. Returns 401/403 if not authenticated or not admin.

nodes.label: Admin Service — getDashboardStats()
nodes.description: Entry point for dashboard data aggregation. Orchestrates 5 parallel queries.

nodes.label: Promise.all() — 5 Parallel Queries
nodes.description: Execute all 5 queries concurrently. If any rejects, entire Promise.all rejects.

nodes.label: Q1: UserModel.countAllUsers()
nodes.description: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM profiles. Total platform user count.

nodes.label: Q2: UserModel.countActiveCreators()
nodes.description: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM profiles WHERE role='creator' AND status='active'. Active content creators.

nodes.label: Q3: TransactionModel.sumPlatformFeeForPeriod(30)
nodes.description: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(platform_fee), 0) FROM transactions WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'. Platform revenue from fees.

nodes.label: Q4: SupportTicketModel.countOpenTickets()
nodes.description: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM support_tickets WHERE status IN ('Open', 'Pending'). Support queue depth.

nodes.label: Q5: UserModel.getNewUsersOverTime(6)
nodes.description: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at), COUNT(*) FROM profiles WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '6 months' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1. User growth trend data.

nodes.label: Aggregate Results
nodes.description: Assemble 5 query results into response object: { totalUsers, activeCreators, platformFees30d, openTickets, newUsersOverTime }.

nodes.label: Return Dashboard Response
nodes.description: JSON response returned to frontend admin dashboard panel.

nodes.label: Frontend: AdminDashboardPanel.tsx — Renders 5 Cards/Charts
nodes.description: Frontend renders dashboard UI: total users card, active creators card, platform revenue card, open tickets card, new users line chart.

nodes.label: Promise.all Rejection — Error Handling
nodes.description: If any one of the 5 queries fails, Promise.all rejects immediately. No partial results delivered.

nodes.label: Return Error Response
nodes.description: Dashboard shows error state. No data displayed. Admin must refresh to retry.

decisions.condition: Do all 5 parallel queries resolve successfully?
decisions.truePath: Aggregate results into response object and return to frontend
decisions.falsePath: Promise.all rejects — return error to frontend with no partial data

errorPaths.trigger: Any single query fails (timeout, connection error, etc.)
errorPaths.destination: Entire Promise.all rejects; dashboard returns error with no data
errorPaths.recovery: Admin refreshes page to retry all 5 queries; no partial success possible

errorPaths.destination: Slow query on large transactions table due to missing index on created_at
errorPaths.recovery: Add composite index on (created_at, platform_fee IS NOT NULL)

errorPaths.trigger: getNewUsersOverTime times out on large profiles table
errorPaths.destination: Dashboard load fails; 6-month aggregation over potentially millions of rows
errorPaths.recovery: Admin retries; consider pre-aggregating user growth data

errorPaths.destination: All 5 queries fail simultaneously due to connection contention
errorPaths.recovery: Admin retries when pool recovers; reduce parallel query count

validationRules: protectAndAdmin middleware required for dashboard endpoint
Dashboard endpoint is read-only — no data modification
Response must include all 5 metric groups (frontend expects specific shape)
businessRules: No caching — every page load runs 5 queries against potentially large tables
No error isolation — Promise.all fails entirely if any single query fails
sumPlatformFeeForPeriod scans transactions table with date range filter — no index on created_at
Dashboard metrics are point-in-time — no historical trend beyond newUsersOverTime
No scheduled pre-aggregation — all aggregations computed live
securityConsiderations: protectAndAdmin enforces admin role on all dashboard data
Dashboard exposes platform-wide financial data (platform fees, user counts, ticket counts)
No admin audit trail — no record of who viewed dashboard or when
No CSRF protection — relies solely on JWT
Query data includes potentially sensitive business metrics (platform revenue)
performanceConsiderations: 5 parallel queries per page load — significant DB load for high-traffic admin usage
No caching layer — every refresh re-runs all queries
COUNT(*) on full profiles table (Q1) — can be slow for large user bases
SUM(platform_fee) with date range (Q3) — no index on created_at leads to full scan
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC + ORDER BY (Q5) — heavy aggregation query
Promise.all creates thundering herd on database — all 5 queries hit simultaneously
